ranking.note: Raised to P1: the fuzz harness reproduced a real relay liveness hole on master and the PR unblocks follow-up fixes in #36506, which is more than the other coverage PRs here.

Raised to P1: framework-level fix for an intermittent flake (#36564) plus removal of manual index-sync boilerplate in 18 tests; flaky-signal fixes are the top concern in this category and this is the broadest one.

Raised to P2 and moved up: fixes actually-failing functional tests on a supported platform and adds a CI FD-limit check, same consequence class as the other flake/platform fixes (#36408, #36529, #35774).

Raised to P2: fuzz coverage of hostile bytes in BIP324 transport receive states is exactly the high-risk p2p-message-handling gap this category ranks just below flaky-signal fixes, on par with #36098/#35000.
Raised to P2 and moved up 17: same problem as #35774 (release-built binaries never exercised in CI) but broader coverage; the two must share a band.
Moved up: a 3-10x throughput gain on an existing slow harness plus a premature-exit fix is the most certain benefit among the P3 speed items.
Placed below the signal and speed fixes; it is a framework capability, which this category ranks after flaky-test and throughput work.
Grouped with the other Boost-migration groundwork (#36091) just below framework-capability work.
Moved up 10 to sit next to #35139 and immediately after #35713, since all three are the same test-framework migration thread.
Opt-in runner integration with no coverage change, so it sits below the harness-signal and migration items.
Moved up 15: structure-aware mutation unlocks deep PSBT deserialization paths and adds reusable mutator dispatch, more consequential than the bench and static-vector P3s.
Moved up 12: it pins a concrete toolchain defect that breaks wallet-migration backups, which beats the purely additive bench/vector items below.
Moved down 14: benchmark fixture modernization ranks below test-signal, framework and fuzz work here, and it directly conflicts with #36254 over the same fixture.
Kept adjacent to #32554 because the two touch the same benchmark block fixture in opposite directions.
Moved down 7: a single wallet benchmark plus helper extraction, grouped with the other bench additions.
Grouped with the other benchmark additions.
Moved down 12: deduplication plus fidelity improvement in existing reorg tests is maintenance-leaning compared with the coverage and speed items above.
Moved down 12: strictly defensive unit-test strengthening for one parser, below the fuzz and bench coverage items.
Preventative harness hardening with no failing test today, so it sits at the bottom of the coverage group.
Lowered to P4: same cleanup as #36606 (already P4) and the author prefers abandoning this automated variant, so it has no stronger claim than the other test-cleanup PRs.

Lowered to P4 and moved down 20: reviewers judged fuzzing wallet RPCs without chain context near-zero efficacy, which makes it weakly justified next to the other fuzz targets (#35964, #36073) kept at P3.

inconsistencies: #32554 and #36254 conflict over the same benchmark fixture: #32554 deletes block413567.raw in favour of a generated block, while #36254 adds undo data for that exact file. Decide the direction on #32554 first; #36254 becomes moot or needs rebasing onto the generator. #32554 also supersedes #32457, and #34360 extracts its own shared fake-block bench helpers that overlap with #32554's generator.

Boost-removal chain: #35139 (new assert macros) and #36091 (operator<< debug output / BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL conversions) are both groundwork for #35713, which itself ships an in-tree framework with BOOST_* shims. Review #35713's framework direction first so #35139/#36091 are not rewritten twice.

#35994 and #36606 are two halves of the same 'declarative transaction construction' cleanup; the #35994 author has said they prefer the manual approach of #36606. Review #36606; #35994 is likely to be closed.
#36437 is a prerequisite for the follow-up orphanage hole fixes in #36506 and should be reviewed before them.
#35442 bundles and depends on #35433 (deprecating the replaceable RPC arguments) and cannot land before it.
#36408, #36529 and #36618 are all CI-flake fixes and are cheapest to review as one batch; #36618 is the framework-wide one and should go first.
#35356 is currently blocked by a real path-handling bug in wallet_signer.py that it exposed; that bug fix is the prerequisite for the CI change, not a reason to deprioritise it.
#35774 and #36082 overlap: both add CI execution of tests against release-built binaries. Decide whether the Guix workflow subsumes the dedicated macOS arm64 job before reviewing both in depth.

#31349 (fails CI on any non-loopback traffic) interacts with #33954 (routes autonomous outbound connections through a local SOCKS5 proxy); confirm the new outbound tests stay on loopback or #31349 will turn them red.
result.notes: The band spread is intentional: two P1s (a real relay-liveness bug found by a new harness, and the framework-wide flake fix), a P2 group covering the Boost-runner project, release-binary CI coverage, high-risk consensus/p2p coverage and the remaining flake/platform fixes, then a broad P3 body of fuzz/bench/framework work, and a long P4 tail of mechanical test cleanups and documentation. Benchmark-only PRs were deliberately clustered in the middle of P3: they are real tooling value but rank below test signal, coverage of risky paths and framework capability in this category.
